owner: CC (the build); Akien (the premise under test — 'if we wind up with a lot of trouble tickets from all the things not working right, i'm ok with that, because that's our to do list', 2026-08-11)
intention: Every envelope the bus carries reaches a device that can consume it — and every place that cannot yet is DERIVED by measurement and marks itself as work, so the catchup to-do list maintains itself instead of being kept by hand.
why: Measured 2026-08-11, and it is the second half of the same silence the postman closed. The bus posted durable envelopes; nothing drained an inbox; BaseShim.deliver stood with zero callers since the day it was written. With the postman built and live-fired, the mail now moves — and the first drain reported that NOTHING ON THE ROSTER CAN TAKE IT: the librarian (the one device with a real receive) refuses every channel that can exist, harbor_master has five envelopes waiting and no device behind its shim, and two envelopes are addressed to a name nothing has ever answered to. Akien, on being shown this: 'we need to make sure all the devices can consume all their messages and that they're not pointed in the wrong place and so on.' THE TRACKING IS HALF THE INTENTION, not a process note: a hand-kept list of broken devices is the stale-list failure he ruled against for the ground loop, and hand-placing a marker at each broken site is that same maintained list in distributed form — a site nobody thought of stays silent forever. So the census DERIVES the list from measurement at one address, and a device added tomorrow gets its red row for free.
traces_to: Law 7 — 'Errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces and permanent in records of truth.' A message that cannot be delivered, failing silently, IS the violation, and it is the trouble lane's founding example in Akien's own words (2026-07-25, carried verbatim in cairn/trouble's charter: 'a poke into nothing, a message that can't be delivered, these are bugs. nothing should fail silently. everything that can't escalate somewhere...'). Also Law 3 (the census is the measurement that turns 'which devices are broken' from a hypothesis into a reading) and Law 9 (the census is precisely the 'site plan showing which lots are still unexcavated' that CLAUDE.md's own Law-9 IOU names as missing).

gates.prove_gate: the tester runs this node's proofs and emits a VALIDATION — verdict and seal from the same hand (TesterDevice().run_proof(..., isolation='netns')). Teeth a hollow build could not pass: the census reds a genuinely unreachable ADDRESSED device; the census stays GREEN on a device nobody mails (the false-red case gets its own tooth, because that is the failure that turns the lane into wallpaper); a raised trouble clears on a measured green; a recurrence writes a FRESH ticket rather than bumping a count.
gates.feeds_back_on_failure: a red criterion at the verdict is a kick-back to the chart chain, not an argument with the gate (Laws 3 + 8)
gates.extra_gates: durability — committed and pushed, verified with git plumbing rather than narration
gates.entry_exit_physics: BUILDME refuses without a berthed chart chain claiming this ticket plus sorted_berth and intent_berth; PROVED refuses without a complete passing verdict artifact; and because the string carries WATCHME, the emission gate refuses the crossing unless the probe is ARMED at the berth named in watchme.probe.

watchme.trigger: Every census run — the event that already fires, since the census is itself what raises and clears the mail lane. The probe reads the trouble store and counts, over mail-* troubles RAISED AFTER THIS NODE'S PROVED CROSSING (the era floor), how many have been cleared by a measured green, the age of each still live, and the prior_attempts on any that recurred. Fires when a mail-* trouble has been live longer than 14 days with its census row still red, or when live mail-* troubles exceed 20 with a rising median age — either being the shape of a lane that accumulates instead of draining.
watchme.enough: CLEARED once the corpus is big enough to judge — >= 8 post-era mail-* troubles raised — AND >= 6 of them reached a measured-green clear, with no live one older than 14 days: the lane demonstrably drains, and a standing watch on a settled question is the re-derivation Law 1 refuses. THE EQUALLY INFORMATIVE OUTCOME IS THE KILL: the lane growing past 20 live with a climbing median age falsifies Akien's 'that's our to do list' premise and says the work needs a different surface than a trouble lane — that outcome retires the watch too, by answering it. THE ERA FLOOR IS LOAD-BEARING and is the lesson of ticket watchme-emits-a-probe: without it the corpus would be the troubles CC raises and clears itself this week, inside this very effort, which measures a motivated builder mid-build and not a self-maintaining lane. Akien may retire the watch by ruling.
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against THIS ticket's falsifier, written through cairn.chart.verdict.write_verdict — the finding names the post-era raised count, the cleared count, the age distribution of the live ones, and any trouble whose prior_attempts shows a fix that did not hold
watchme.nexus: hypothesize — the tree that remembers what killed which. This node's load-bearing claim is a PREDICTION about whether a self-maintaining marker lane causes work to happen, and a prediction that did not hold belongs there.
watchme.consumer: AKIEN, through the owner's gate. The premise under test is his, stated in his own words, so a measured 'the lane accumulated and nobody worked it' is a spec-changing input and not a detail. The probe deposits and pokes; it has NO authority to back-edge this node (Law 6).
watchme.probe_note: BERTH NAMED AT TICKETING because the emission gate measures ARMED from a path (cairn/base/watchme_spec.py). The path is a COMMITMENT, not a claim the file exists; it does not yet. It berths with what it watches — orient owns the census that raises and clears the mail lane, so the property under test lives with the mechanism under test.

amendments.ruling: addressable but unreachable... outside of bugs, or things we haven't built yet... every device, including the bus itself and the ground loop, has a presence on the bus and can respond to a health query... so the basics of this has to be in the base shim. As to census... what census?
amendments.what_it_killed: THE CENSUS, entirely. This ticket proposed measuring code structure — does a device's class declare receive, which channels does it accept — as the way to find unreachable devices. If every device answers a health query, that is a PROXY read instead of the thing: you ask the running device rather than reading its class. cairn/orient's own charter names that exact failure as its founding why ('a proxy was read instead of the thing'), and the census was proposed inside orient. Withdrawn, not defended.
amendments.what_it_also_killed: This ticket's own assumption-kill. It had ruled that 'a device nobody addresses needs no receive, so red means ADDRESSED-BUT-UNREACHABLE, never lacks-receive'. Akien's spec is stronger and simpler: EVERY device — the bus and the ground loop included — is addressable and answers. There is no legitimate non-answerer, so unreachable is red universally, and the two exceptions he names (bugs, things not yet built) are exactly the things that SHOULD be red. Law 9 falls out rather than being applied by hand.
amendments.what_survives: The aim, and every repair child. Mail arriving is one case of a device being reachable; the tracking half moves to the successor node, where the health sweep — ask every device on the roster, no answer is red — does what the census was invented to do, with no code measurement at all.
amendments.successor: the presence protocol (every device answers a standard verb set, reachable identically from CLI, bus and web) — its own /intent, this ticket's parent once cast

open_questions: RESOLVED BY THE AMENDMENT — 'what event fires the census' is moot; there is no census. The live form of the question moves to the successor node: at what CADENCE is the health query asked. It is real there, because asking everyone every beat is a poll, and yet asking IS the measurement (you cannot learn a device is alive by waiting for it to fail). A /chart decompose question, not a guess.

MAY A MEASUREMENT AUTO-CLEAR A TROUBLE? Survives the amendment unchanged. The trouble lane's clear is per-recipient and demands what_changed, and was designed around a human witness naming the fix. A measurement in that slot is arguably stronger evidence, but it changes what prior_attempts counts — flaps rather than failed fixes. Left open deliberately; it is a /chart question.
